commits.title: runJobs() hands each job a report(error): logged, and the run counted as failed once its other parts have run

changes.how: (1) Export `export type JobReport = (error: unknown, part?: string) => void;` and `export const logOnly: JobReport = (error, part) => log("error", "cron.job_part_failed", { part: part ?? null }, error);` (what an entry function uses when it is called outside the dispatcher: a test, a person's action). (2) Change `tracked` to `export async function tracked<T>(job: string, everySeconds: number, run: (report: JobReport) => Promise<T>): Promise<T | null>`. Inside: `const reported: { part: string | null; error: unknown }[] = [];` and `const report: JobReport = (error, part) => { reported.push({ part: part ?? null, error }); log("error", "cron.job_part_failed", { job, part: part ?? null }, error); };`. Call `const result = await run(report);`. Then, when `reported.length === 0`, `await record(job, everySeconds, started, null)` as today; otherwise `await record(job, everySeconds, started, new Error(`${reported.length} part(s) failed (${reported.map((r) => r.part ?? "?").join(", ")})`, { cause: reported[0].error }))` (record() already writes an Error's cause into the message). In both cases `return result`: a job whose part failed still answers what its other parts did. The existing `catch` branch (the job threw) stays as it is. Callers that pass `() => x()` keep compiling: a function may take fewer parameters. (3) Change `runJobs`'s type to `J extends Record<string, (report: JobReport) => Promise<unknown>>` and its call to `tracked(`${prefix}.${kebab(name)}`, everySeconds, (report) => jobs[name](report))`. (4) Add `export function trackedWork<T>(route: string, everySeconds: number, run: (report: JobReport) => Promise<T>): Promise<T | null> { return tracked(`${route}.work`, everySeconds, run); }` with the comment: the work a route does after answering (`after()`), kept as a job of its own, since the route's own row records only that it answered. (5) Update the file's header comment: a job that throws, or reports a caught error, is logged and recorded as failed, and the others finish.

Add two cases in the file's style (jobs named with its `prefix`, console.error silenced as the first case does). Case A `a job whose first part fails still runs its second part, and its run is counted as failed`: `let second = false; const answer = await tracked(job, 300, async (report) => { try { throw new Error("mail down"); } catch (error) { report(error, "first"); } second = true; return 5; });` expect `answer` 5, `second` true, and the row `{ failures: 1 }` with `lastError` containing `1 part(s) failed (first)` and `mail down`; a following clean run sets failures back to 0. The same through `runJobs(prefix, 300, { a: async (report) => { report(new Error("x"), "p"); return 1; }, b: async () => 2 })`: the answer is `{ a: 1, b: 2 }`, row `${prefix}.a` failed and `${prefix}.b` ok. Case B `a runner that throws after the answer leaves the route's work failed`: `await trackedWork(`${prefix}.page-jobs`, 60, async () => { throw new Error("model down"); });` expect the row `${prefix}.page-jobs.work` with failures 1. Then one more assertion with the real name the step asks for: `await trackedWork("route.page-jobs", 60, async () => { throw new Error("model down"); })` leaves `route.page-jobs.work` with failures at least 1; delete that row in the test's clean-up (`delete from commerce.cron_jobs where job = 'route.page-jobs.work'`).
